name: endosymbiosis
title: The Endosymbiotic Transition — enclosure mechanics (S3)
question: Can an archaeal-like deformable host physically surround and enclose a bacterial partner purely from differential adhesion, and under which mechanical conditions does wrapping reach a stable topology rather than a partial cup or a transient contact? This is the viva-cpm realization of gate G3 (Enclosure) of the viva-genesis eukaryogenesis campaign "The Endosymbiotic Transition" (campaign composite B — active membrane mechanics).
hypothesis: On a Cellular Potts lattice, the host engulfs the symbiont when host-symbiont adhesion beats the combined surface-tension cost (J_hs < J_sM - J_hM). Sweeping those mechanical energies traces a phase diagram with a sharp transition between no enclosure, partial wrapping, transient internalization, and stable enclosure — stable wrapping as an emergent outcome, not an imposed threshold.

executive.what_is_this: The physical-enclosure plane of the endosymbiosis phase diagram, computed on the real Rust CPM engine. One parameterized composite (protrusion_enclosure) runs the host/symbiont wrapping model; a 2-axis sweep over adhesion and symbiont surface tension classifies the enclosure regime at each point.
executive.verdict: Differential adhesion alone is sufficient for stable enclosure in a well-defined mechanical regime; the measured transition tracks the predicted J_hs = J_sM - J_hM line.
executive.verdict_detail: Companion to the viva-genesis eukaryogenesis investigation (gate G3). Demonstrates that primitive engulfment can precede dedicated phagocytic machinery.

scientific_argument.main_claim: A deformable host cell reaches stable enclosure of a partner by differential adhesion alone, with a sharp mechanical transition, giving the G3 gate an emergent spatial readout.

findings.statement: Differential adhesion alone drives stable enclosure in a well-defined mechanical regime: the adhesion x symbiont-surface-tension phase diagram shows a sharp transition tracking J_hs = J_sM - J_hM, with stable enclosure, partial wrapping, transient internalization, and no enclosure as distinct regimes.

studies.claim: Differential adhesion alone drives a deformable host to stable enclosure of a symbiont in a well-defined mechanical regime (J_hs below the J_sM - J_hM threshold); below the transition the host forms only a partial cup or leaves the symbiont free.
